findings.title: Existing local recovery-code credentials are not cleared when a federated credential is created
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential treats a true return from user.credentialManager().updateCredential() as sufficient and does not remove any existing local recovery-authn-codes credentials. If a federated user already had a local recovery-code credential, generating new codes in the user storage can leave the old local credential in place. Because validation can consider existing stored credentials, previously issued codes may remain valid after rotation, breaking the expected one-time/replace semantics.

findings.title: Plaintext recovery codes are passed to user storage
findings.body: The helper serializes the raw generated recovery codes and sends them to the user storage provider. The local path stores only hashed codes, but this federated path exposes plaintext bearer secrets to the storage implementation. A storage that simply persists the supplied challenge response will retain recoverable plaintext codes. It would be safer to pass a hashed representation, or make the hashed-storage contract explicit, rather than handing out raw codes.

findings.title: Test storage permits replay of recovery codes
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid compares the submitted recovery code with the stored list but never removes or marks the code as used. Recovery codes are one-time credentials, so this test storage allows the same code to be replayed indefinitely. The added test only uses a code once, so it does not catch this. The test storage should consume the code on successful validation and the test should assert reuse fails.

findings.title: Federated recovery credential is returned without a stable ID
findings.body: getCredentials constructs the recovery credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues but does not copy the stable ID from the stored CredentialModel. If the returned credential has a null or newly generated ID on each call, Keycloak features that delete or reference the credential by ID, such as cleaning up exhausted recovery codes or account-console credential management, will not work reliably for this storage.

findings.title: Unsafe Optional.get can cause a 500 if recovery credential is absent
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns Optional, but the bean immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the credential is missing because of a race, a misconfigured flow, or a storage provider returning no credential, the login page rendering fails with NoSuchElementException instead of handling the absent-credential state gracefully.

findings.title: Missing coverage for recovery-code consumption and fallback behavior
findings.body: The new test only covers setup and one successful login with the first federated recovery code. It does not verify that used codes are consumed, that exhausting all codes triggers CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES, or that local storage is used when a user storage provider does not support recovery codes. Those are core behaviors introduced by this PR.
